'''Jeremy Griffith''' (born 1945) is an Australian author.<ref>{{cite news|title=Baggage check|work=The Weekend Australian|publisher=News Corp|location=Canberra, ACT, Australia|author=Conway, Ronald|date=19 July 2003| page=B10}}</ref>{{r|clark smh}} He first came to public attention for his attempts to find the [[Tasmanian tiger]]. He later became noted for his writings on the [[human condition]] and theories about human progress,{{r|bissland}} which seek to give a biological, rational explanation of human behaviour.{{r|nicklin}} He founded the not-for-profit Fix The World in 1983.

==Early life and career==

Griffith was raised on a sheep property in central [[New South Wales]].{{r|nicklin}} He was educated at [[Tudor House School]], New South Wales, and the [[Geelong Grammar School]], [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], in 1965 completing the [[Higher School Certificate (New South Wales)|NSW Higher School Leaving Certificate]] with first class honours in biology.<ref>{{cite news|title=Leaving Certificate Results |work=The Sydney Morning Herald|publisher=Fairfax Media|location=Sydney, NSW, Australia|date=14 January 1965|url=|page=16}}</ref> He began a science degree at the [[University of New England (Australia)|University of New England]], in northern New South Wales, and completed his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in zoology at the [[University of Sydney]] in 1971.{{r|denial 04|p=528}}<ref>[https://www.jeremygriffith.com/biography/ "Biographical Profile"]. ''Jeremy Griffith'' website. 2023.</ref>

=== Search for the Tasmanian Tiger ===
Griffith first became known for his search for surviving [[Tasmanian tiger]]s, or thylacines,<ref name="ag elusive">{{Cite magazine| author= Park, Andy|title= Tasmanian Tiger – Extinct or merely elusive?|journal= [[Australian Geographic]] |volume= 1|issue=3 |pages= 66–83| date=July 1986}}</ref> the last known specimen of which had died in captivity in 1936. The search was conducted from 1967 to 1973.<ref name="NatHist">{{Cite magazine| last= Griffith| first= Jeremy|title= The Search for the Tasmanian Tiger|magazine= [[Natural History (magazine)|Natural History]]|date=December 1972| issue= 81| publisher= [[American Museum of Natural History]] |pages= 70–77}}</ref> It is considered the most intensive search to that point,{{r|ag elusive}} and included exhaustive surveys along Tasmania's west coast,<ref name="NatHist" /> installation of automatic camera stations, prompt investigations of claimed sightings,{{r|paddle}} and in 1972 the creation of the Thylacine Expeditionary Research Team with [[Bob Brown]]. It concluded without finding any evidence of the animal's continuing existence, despite numerous claimed ongoing sightings.{{r|ag elusive}} Griffith's search was the subject of an episode of ABC TV's ''[[A Big Country]]'';<ref>{{Cite book |last=Downes |first=Jim |title=A Big Country: Stories of Australia & its people from the ABC-TV series |publisher=Angus & Robertson; ABC Enterprises |year=1988 |isbn=978-0-207-15896-4 |pages=31–36}}
* "Tiger Country". ''A Big Country''. ABC TV. 1973.</ref> and his report of the search was published in [[Natural History (magazine)|''Natural History'']].<ref name="NatHist" /><ref>{{cite book |last1=Smith |first1=M. |editor1-last=Archer |editor1-first=Michael |title=Carnivorous Marsupials |date=Feb 1982 |publisher=Royal Zoological Society of NSW |isbn=978-0-9599951-3-8 |pages=237–253 |chapter=Review of the Thylacine (Marsupialia, Thylacinidae)}}</ref>

Some ten years later the thylacine was declared extinct by the [[International Union for Conservation of Nature]] in 1982<ref name="IUCN">{{cite iucn | author = Burbidge, A. A. | author2 = Woinarski, J. | title = ''Thylacinus cynocephalus'' | journal = [[IUCN Red List of Threatened Species]] | volume = 2016 | article-number = e.T21866A21949291 | year = 2016 | url = https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/21866/21949291 | doi = 10.2305/IUCN.UK.2016-2.RLTS.T21866A21949291.en | access-date = 16 December 2019}}</ref> and by the Tasmanian government in 1986.<ref name="paddle">{{cite book|title=The Last Tasmanian Tiger: The History and Extinction of the Thylacine|first=Robert |last=Paddle|year=2000|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|page=197|isbn=0-521-53154-3}}</ref>

=== Furniture business ===
After returning from his search for the thylacine, Griffith started a furniture business, Griffith Tablecraft, with his brother Gervase. The business made simple furniture out of solid slabs of wood without use of nails or glue. Griffith left the company in 1990 and it was ultimately sold in 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Griffith Tablecraft |url=https://www.humancondition.com/griffith-tablecraft/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=FIX THE WORLD |language=en}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=July 2026}}

==On human nature, the human condition, and progress==
Griffith began writing on the human condition in 1975. His books seek to give a biological and rational explanation of human behaviour{{r|nicklin}} and include references to philosophical and religious sources.<ref name="bissland">{{cite news |author=Bissland, Helen |date=1 November 2003 |title=Delving into the human mindset of denial |work=The Southland Times |location=Invercargill, New Zealand |page=35}}</ref>

His first book on the subject, ''Free: The End of the Human Condition,'' was published in 1988,<ref name="Free">{{cite book| author=Griffith, Jeremy| title= Free: The End of the Human Condition| year= 1988|publisher= WTM Publishing & Communications Pty Ltd|page=228|isbn=0-7316-0495-4}}</ref> and Griffith was interviewed by [[Caroline Jones (broadcaster)|Caroline Jones]] on her [[Radio National]] program, ''[[The Search for Meaning (radio program)|The Search for Meaning]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Trove |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/work/23222687/version/28141876 |access-date=2025-05-08 |website=trove.nla.gov.au}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Caroline Jones interviewing Jeremy Griffith |url=https://www.humancondition.com/jeremy-griffith-interview-with-caroline-jones/ |access-date=2025-05-08 |website=Fix The World |language=en}}</ref> ''A Species In Denial'' (2003) became a bestseller in Australia and New Zealand.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bestsellers books|work=The Newcastle Herald |location=Newcastle, New South Wales, Australia|author=Sprogis, Elvira|date=21 June 2003| page=15}}</ref> ''{{'}}Freedom{{'}}: The End of the Human Condition'' (2016) has been described as the definitive presentation of his treatise.<ref name=":0">{{Cite magazine |title=The Psychological Rehabilitation of the Human Race |first=Harry |last=Prosen |date=July 2021 |url=https://www.themontrealreview.com/2009/The-psychological-rehabilitation-of-the-human-race.php |access-date=2021-07-23 |magazine=The Montréal Review}}</ref><ref name="gLuck">{{cite magazine|last=Luck|first=Geoffrey |title=The Hubris of ''Four Corners''|magazine=[[Quadrant (magazine)|Quadrant]]|date=November 2012 |volume=LVI|issue=11 |url=http://www.quadrant.org.au/magazine/issue/2012/11/the-hubris-of-four-corners|access-date=1 November 2018}}</ref>

In support of his theory, he cites from a broad selection of sources, including many thinkers he regards as "unevasive" or "contemporary prophets", including [[James Ralph Darling|James Darling]], [[Charles Darwin]], [[Sigmund Freud]], [[Carl Jung]], [[Thomas Henry Huxley|Thomas Huxley]], [[Stephen Hawking]] and [[Laurens van der Post]].<ref name="nicklin">{{Cite magazine |last=Nicklin |first=Lenore |date=21 April 1998 |title=Higher Ground |url=https://images.wtmfiles.com/1998-05-21-TheBulletin-HigherGround_WEB_909x600.jpg |access-date=6 January 2023 |magazine=The Bulletin |pages=28–29}}</ref><ref name="denial 04">{{Cite book |last=Griffith |first=Jeremy |title=A Species In Denial |date=2004 |publisher=WTM Publishing and Communications |isbn=978-1-74129-001-1}}</ref>

Griffith explains [[human nature]] (what he terms the [[human condition]]) by proposing that as consciousness emerged in our [[hominid|hominid ancestors]], the intellect's experiments in self-management were in effect criticised by our pre-established instincts, the result of which was that humans unavoidably became increasingly "angry, egocentric and alienated".{{r|gravity|superior 25}} 

According to psychologist [[Ronald Conway]], Griffith holds that we are at war with our own selves, causing humanity to become alienated from its original peaceful state of innocence. Griffith says that this war within is the cause of ongoing actual wars and the general lack of cooperation in the world.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Conway |first=Ronald |title=Book Review: A Species in Denial |journal=Australian Quarterly Journal of Contemporary Analysis |edition=January–February 2004 |jstor=20638236| page=37}}</ref> Griffith analyses the scientific literature in human evolution; rejects claims that human ancestors were brutal and aggressive; and instead points to fossil evidence such as that of ''[[Ardipithecus ramidus]]'', and primatological studies of [[Bonobo|bonobos]] in support of his thesis that ancient humans were a gentle, loving and co-operative species.<ref name="clark smh">{{cite news|title=Biologist Jeremy Griffith examines where the human race is headed|work=The Sydney Morning Herald|publisher=Fairfax Media |author=Clark, Gary|date=6 October 2014|url=https://www.smh.com.au/education/biologist-jeremy-griffith-examines-where-the-human-race-is-headed-20141006-10qyvm.html |access-date=1 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bonobos provide living evidence of love-indoctrination process {{!}} FREEDOM |url=https://www.humancondition.com/freedom-bonobos-show-living-evidence-of-love-indoctrination/ |access-date=2026-05-07 |website=FIX THE WORLD |language=en}}</ref>

In a 2020 article "The fury of the left, explained", published in ''[[The Spectator Australia]],'' Griffith argued that the ideology of [[Left-wing politics|the Left]] is dangerous to humanity's progress. He describes left-wing views as regressive and likely to lead to extinction.<ref name="fury">{{Cite magazine |url= https://www.spectator.com.au/2020/02/the-fury-of-the-left-explained/  |access-date=2020-02-10 |title=The fury of the left, explained |date=2020-02-05 |magazine=The Spectator Australia |language=en-us |archive-date=5 February 2020 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200205081024/https://www.spectator.com.au/2020/02/the-fury-of-the-left-explained/ |last=Griffith |first=Jeremy}}</ref>

==Fix The World==
Fix The World was founded by Griffith in 1983 as the Centre for Humanity's Adulthood, an organisation dedicated to developing and promoting understanding of the human condition. It was incorporated in 1990 with Griffith and his colleague, mountaineer [[Tim Macartney-Snape]], among its founding directors and became a registered charity in New South Wales in 1990{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}, known as the Foundation for Humanity's Adulthood. In 2009, its name changed to the World Transformation Movement<ref>{{Cite web |title=History of FIX THE WORLD |url=https://www.humancondition.com/history-of-fix-the-world/ |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=FIX THE WORLD |language=en}}</ref> and then to Fix The World in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Press Release on Reuters: FIX THE WORLD’s Rebranding |url=https://www.humancondition.com/reuters-press-release-name-change/ |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=FIX THE WORLD |language=en}}</ref>

==Reception==

A reviewer of Griffith's book ''A Species in Denial'' described its thesis as "humanity is in denial about the loss of its innocence in a corrupt and broken world", and believed it would have benefited from including discussion of the works of [[Martin Buber]], [[H. Richard Niebuhr]], [[Lawrence Kohlberg]] and [[James W. Fowler]], who also examine the moral stages of human growth.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cohen |first=John |title=Book Review: A Species In Denial |url= |journal=Reading Time |edition=May 2004 |publisher=Children's Book Council of Australia |via=EBSCO}}</ref>

Some reviewers described ''A Species in Denial'' as challenging<ref>{{Cite news |date=20 September 2004 |title=High time to fess up |url= |work=Gold Coast Bulletin |page=W13 |via=NewsBank}}</ref> or “a difficult book to read, but through the repetition of his concepts the reader finally grasps Griffith’s meaning and, surprisingly, when this happens all kinds of questions arise, which is refreshing".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Steel |first=David |date=4 October 2004 |title=Are we in critical condition? A new book by controversial biologist Jeremy Griffith challenges our ideals as human beings. |url= |work=Townsville Bulletin |page=58 |via=NewsBank}}</ref> Conway wrote "A Species In Denial needs repeated reading, not because it is particularly difficult but because it goes against so much of the resigned don't-rock-the-boat attitude of the Western mind in particular."<ref name=":1" />

One reviewer criticised Griffith's analysis of the anthropological data to support the notion that humanity had a cooperative past, highlighting his reliance on the writings of controversial figures, like the South African philosopher Sir [[Laurens van der Post]], and [[ǃKung people|!Kung]] [[San peoples|Bushman]] researcher [[Elizabeth Marshall Thomas]].<ref name="clark smh" />

It has also been suggested that despite agreeing with the broad thrust of Griffith's thesis, some will disagree with his high opinion of the Scottish psychiatrist [[R. D. Laing]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ireland |first=Alan |date=3 October 2003 |title=Book attempts to find the elusive light |work=The Manawatu Standard}}</ref>

===Media coverage and legal proceedings===
In 1995, Griffith, Macartney-Snape and the Foundation for Humanity's Adulthood (Fix The World's name at the time) were the subject of an [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]] (ABC) ''[[Four Corners (Australian TV program)|Four Corners]]'' programme{{r|gLuck}} and an article in the ''[[Sydney Morning Herald]]'' (''SMH'') newspaper{{r|kux}} in which it was alleged that Macartney-Snape used speaking appearances at schools to promote the foundation, and that Griffith "publishes work of such a poor standard that it has no support at all from the scientific community". In [[Defamation in Australia|defamation actions]] against the ABC and the ''SMH'', the allegations were ruled to be false and the pieces defamatory.<ref name="NSWSC 764">{{cite AustLII|litigants=Griffith & Macartney-Snape v Australian Broadcasting Corporation |court= NSWSC|num=764|year=2008 |pinpoint=|date=1 August 2008|courtname=Supreme Court of New South Wales |juris=NSW, Australia }}</ref>

In 1998, following a complaint by Griffith and Macartney-Snape, the [[Australian Broadcasting Authority]] censured the ABC for unbalanced and inaccurate reporting and breaching the ABC code of practice, with ''[[The Bulletin (Australian periodical)|The Bulletin]]'' describing the ''Four Corners'' programme as a "[[wikt:hatchet job|hatchet job]]" (another term for a "hit piece").{{r|nicklin}}

Griffith, Macartney-Snape and Fix The World sued the ABC and the ''Sydney Morning Herald'' in the [[NSW Supreme Court]] and both publications were found to be defamatory.<ref name="kux">{{cite journal|last=Kux|first=Y. C.|title=Jeremy Griffith & Ors v John Fairfax Publications Pty Ltd and David Millikan|journal=Gazette of Law & Journalism|date=29 September 2005}}</ref><ref name="Drummond">{{cite news|last=Drummond|first=Andrew|title=Half-million payout for ABC defamation|url=http://news.smh.com.au/national/halfmillion-payout-for-abc-defamation-20080801-3ogo.html|access-date=10 October 2011|newspaper=The Sydney Morning Herald|date=1 August 2008}}</ref> In 2008, the ABC was ordered to pay Macartney-Snape almost $500,000 in damages, and with costs, the payout was expected to exceed $1 million.<ref name="Drummond" /> While the jury found that what the ABC said about Griffith was defamatory, the judge dismissed the case after the defences of truth, qualified privilege and comment were considered.{{r|NSWSC 764|Drummond}} Griffith appealed that decision to the [[New South Wales Court of Appeal]], which dismissed the appeal<ref name="NSWCA 257">{{cite AustLII|litigants=Griffith & Macartney-Snape v Australian Broadcasting Corporation |court= NSWCA|num=257|year=2010|pinpoint=|date=7 October 2010|courtname=New South Wales Court of Appeal |juris=NSW, Australia |ref= }}</ref> on the basis of qualified privilege and comment being upheld, but found that the defamatory allegation about Griffith was not justified.{{r|gLuck|NSWSC 764|def law}} The court case against the ''Sydney Morning Herald'' was resolved in 2009 when it published an apology to Fix The World for the harm caused by the publication.<ref>{{cite news|title=Apology|newspaper=The Sydney Morning Herald|date=6 June 2009}}</ref>
